Candied Sweet Potatoes

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 45 min

Candied sweet potatoes are a classic Thanksgiving side dish in the United States, known for their rich, sweet flavor and tender texture. This dish combines tender sweet potatoes with a buttery, brown sugar glaze, often enhanced with warm spices, making it a comforting and festive addition to the holiday table.

Ingredients

  • 4 large sweet potatoes (about 3 pounds / 1.4 kg), peeled and sliced into 1/2-inch (1.3 cm) rounds
  • 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
  • 3/4 cup packed brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup water
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Optional: 1/2 cup chopped pecans or marshmallows for topping

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Place the sliced sweet potatoes in a large baking dish in an even layer.
  3. In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
  4. Add the brown sugar, water, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt to the melted butter and stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is smooth.
  5. Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
  6. Pour the brown sugar mixture evenly over the sweet potatoes.
  7. Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
  8. Remove the foil and bake for an additional 15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the sauce is bubbly.
  9. If desired, sprinkle chopped pecans or marshmallows over the top and bake uncovered for 5 more minutes until toasted or melted.
  10. Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, try adding a tablespoon of maple syrup to the glaze.
  • If you prefer a less sweet dish, reduce the brown sugar to 1/2 cup.
  • To save time, you can boil the sweet potato slices for 5 minutes before baking to speed up cooking.
